content.text:
`stepsSummary` (`src/control/dashboard.ts:1726`) folds a run of tool calls into one line. For each call it looks up the tool in `toolLooks` (`:1653`), which gives an action (read, command, change, search, subagent and so on) and the argument naming the file. Calls are grouped by action. A file counts once however often it's touched, so an edit and a write to one path make one changed file. A tool with no look becomes its own action, named as it is. Actions are sorted by priority, and the first `phrasesShown` (3) are phrased, like "Ran 2 commands, read 2 files". Whatever is left collapses into "used another tool" or "used N other tools".

The tests are the four fold-related ones at `src/control/dashboard.test.ts:796`, `:833`, `:854` and `:1484`, plus the Claude transcript test at `:1384`. All pass as is, and no build was needed.

With `phrasesShown` set to 2, five of the seven matched tests fail. The cause is that a third action gets swallowed into the "other tools" count. For example, "read a file" or "searched the code" turns into "used another tool", and "ran a subagent" does the same. I then set it back to 3. The file now matches HEAD and nothing is committed.

content.text:
Only one tool name in `src/fixtures/claude-transcript.jsonl` has no entry in `toolLooks`: `mcp__notes-compaction__notes`, called once. `jq` isn't installed, so I used grep. It finds 6 `tool_use` blocks, and the names are `Bash` (3), `Agent`, `Write` and the MCP tool.

In a fold, `stepsSummary` treats a tool with no entry as its own action. It uses the `unknownTool` phrase at `src/control/dashboard.ts:1639`, with the raw name and priority 2, below every known action. Today it reads:

- **Alone:** "used mcp__notes-compaction__notes", or "used mcp__notes-compaction__notes 2 times" for repeat calls.
- **Past the third phrase:** it collapses into "used another tool", since priority 2 sorts last.
- **Fixture's fold:** it has only three distinct actions, so the MCP tool would fall outside the shown phrases, and it already reads "Changed a file, ran a command, used another tool". That matches the failing output from the `phrasesShown = 2` run, where the MCP tool is shown as "used another tool".

Its row inside the fold has no `subject` from `toolLooks`. It falls back to the first of `command`, `pattern`, `path` or `url` that the call has as a string argument. If none is present, the row has no subject.

1626	// After t3code's summarizeToolGroup. Copyright (c) 2026 T3 Tools Inc., MIT licence; see THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md.
1627	type Action = "command" | "change" | "subagent" | "read" | "search" | "web" | "fetch" | "todo";
1628	interface Phrase { priority: number; one: string; many: (n: number) => string }
1629	const actions: Record<Action, Phrase> = {
1630	  command: { priority: 0, one: "ran a command", many: (n) => `ran ${n} commands` },
1631	  change: { priority: 0, one: "changed a file", many: (n) => `changed ${n} files` },
1632	  subagent: { priority: 0, one: "ran a subagent", many: (n) => `ran ${n} subagents` },
1633	  read: { priority: 1, one: "read a file", many: (n) => `read ${n} files` },
1634	  search: { priority: 1, one: "searched the code", many: (n) => `searched the code ${n} times` },
1635	  web: { priority: 1, one: "searched the web", many: (n) => `searched the web ${n} times` },
1636	  fetch: { priority: 1, one: "fetched a page", many: (n) => `fetched ${n} pages` },
1637	  todo: { priority: 1, one: "updated the to-do list", many: (n) => `updated the to-do list ${n} times` },
1638	};
1639	const unknownTool = (name: string): Phrase => ({ priority: 2, one: `used ${name}`, many: (n) => `used ${name} ${n} times` });
1640	
1641	/**
1642	 * How a tool's calls read, by its name, pi's in lower case and Claude Code's capitalized: the argument that says what
1643	 * a call did, shown in its row, one shown whole as text, what it changes, the argument naming the file it acts on,
1644	 * so a fold counts a file once, and the action a fold counts it under.
1645	 */
1646	interface ToolLook {
1647	  subject?: string;
1648	  text?: string;
1649	  diff?: (args: Args) => Diff | null;
1650	  file?: string;
1651	  action?: Action;
1652	}
1653	const toolLooks: Readonly<Record<string, ToolLook>> = {
1654	  read: { subject: "path", file: "path", action: "read" },
1655	  bash: { subject: "command", action: "command" },
1656	  edit: { subject: "path", file: "path", diff: editsDiff("oldText", "newText"), action: "change" },
1657	  write: { subject: "path", file: "path", diff: contentDiff, action: "change" },
1658	  grep: { subject: "pattern", action: "search" },
1659	  find: { subject: "pattern", action: "search" },

The change worked, and I've reverted it. Nothing is committed.

  - Added `"mcp__notes-compaction__notes": { action: "notes" }` to `toolLooks`.
- **Mistake and fix:** I first typed the key with underscores (`mcp__notes_compaction__notes`). I corrected it to the hyphenated name before running anything, so no test or typecheck run used the wrong key.
- **Tests:** `node --test --test-name-pattern=fold src/control/dashboard.test.ts` passed all 7 tests.
- **Typecheck:** `npm run typecheck` ran clean.
- **Diff:** `git diff --stat` showed `src/control/dashboard.ts | 4 +++-`, with 3 insertions and 1 deletion. After `git checkout src/control/dashboard.ts` the tree has no changes apart from the untracked `node_modules`.

None of the existing tests exercises the notes action. The fixture's MCP call sits in the transcript test, which still passed, so that test presumably doesn't assert the fold line for it. A real change would need a test asserting "took notes".
